proposal.title: Tina Peters Says White House Counsel Worked to Secure Her Release
proposal.description_short: Tina Peters says White House counsel helped with her clemency; reporting leaves his precise role unconfirmed.
proposal.description_medium: Former Mesa County clerk Tina Peters said on the Stern American podcast on August 13, 2026, that White House counsel David Warrington worked with the Trump administration and Colorado Gov. Jared Polis to secure her release, the Grand Junction Sentinel reported. The Denver Post later reported that Peters’ attorney said Warrington helped with communications with Polis, while the governor’s office said it had no records mentioning Warrington. The reporting leaves Warrington’s precise role unconfirmed.
proposal.description_long: On August 13, 2026, former Mesa County clerk Tina Peters said on the Stern American podcast that White House counsel David Warrington had worked with the Trump administration and Colorado Gov. Jared Polis to secure her release, according to the Grand Junction Sentinel’s August 15 report. The Colorado governor’s office had commuted Peters’ sentence, with parole effective June 1, 2026, according to the state’s clemency announcement. The Denver Post later reported that Peters’ attorney said Warrington helped with communications with Polis. The Post also reported that the governor’s office did not directly answer whether Polis had communicated with Warrington or President Donald Trump about Peters and said it had no records mentioning Warrington. Peters’ statement is an attributed claim, not independent proof that White House officials arranged or caused the commutation. These reports do not establish the exact nature of any contacts or a quid pro quo, so the record is limited to Peters’ public account and the subsequent reporting about the unresolved role of Warrington.

supports: Peters’s August 13 podcast statement attributing work toward her release to Warrington and the administration; the Grand Junction Sentinel’s account published August 15.
does_not_establish: That White House personnel actually arranged or caused the commutation.

supports: Peters’s attorney’s statement that Warrington helped with communications; the governor’s office had no records mentioning Warrington and did not directly answer contact questions; the reported June 1 release date.
does_not_establish: A confirmed contact between Trump/Warrington and Polis or a causal role in the clemency decision.

supports: Polis’s commutation of Peters and June 1, 2026 parole effective date.
